To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PDN resonances can be triggered by software and micro-architecture interactions and the PDN resonant frequency can be tuned by varying the on-die capacitance.

(a) we have demonstrated the first system-level PDN characterization of an ARM Cortex-A57 processor, (b) we have identified the key contributors to the PDN resonances, (c) we have shown that these resonances can cause system failure, and (d) we have proposed a mitigation technique to address the resonances.

1) the system-level PDN can be modeled using a simple RLC model and the resulting model can predict the system-level behavior; 2) a dual-core 28nm Cortex-A57 cluster is susceptible to pathological AC PDN resonances and the resulting transients can cause system failure; 3) these transients are primarily caused by the interactions between the micro-architecture, software and the PDN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
characterizing the system-level PDN and its impact on system-level performance, and we present a methodology to mitigate the impact of the PDN on system performance.
